text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A organizes three distinct reasons into separate body paragraphs with a clear introduction and conclusion restating the position", "quality": "Organizational structure", "description": "The essay presents a clear thesis and develops each supporting reason in its own paragraph, framed by an introduction and conclusion."}, {"evidence": "Essay A quotes the article directly for each reason, e.g., \"Google cars aren't truly driverless\" and \"The car can handle driving functions at speeds up to 25 mph\"", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay grounds each argument in specific quoted details from the source article rather than paraphrasing vaguely."}, {"evidence": "Essay A states its position clearly at the start and returns to it in the conclusion, e.g., \"I wouldnt like to have one of these driverless cars\"", "quality": "Clear position statement", "description": "The essay maintains a consistent, explicit stance throughout that the reader can easily follow."}, {"evidence": "Essay A reasons through each point, e.g., explaining that if the car still requires the driver to take over, it defeats the purpose of a driverless car", "quality": "Reasoned elaboration", "description": "The essay explains the logic behind each objection rather than merely asserting it, connecting the evidence to the argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay B's body paragraphs wander between points without developing a focused argument and its conclusion introduces new claims not argued earlier", "quality": "Focused argument development", "description": "Essay A keeps each argument tied to its stated reason, whereas Essay B drifts across loosely connected ideas."}]}
